title: Sprint check-in: UI / Rollouts / Analytics — 2026-03-18
content:
Purpose: quick cross-subteam check-in for Console & Tooling. Focus: unblock the UI canary, finalize rollout gating metrics, and align analytics events for A/B evaluation.

Attendees:
- Maya Chen (owner)
- Arjun Rao (frontend)
- Sofia Martinez (product/rollouts)
- Leo Park (analytics)
- Ran out to sync with infra briefly: Chris and Nina dropped status in thread.

High-level summary:
- Canary deploy of console-ui v3.14 showed a subtle client-side regression only on Chrome Canary builds: preview modal sometimes reflows and increases perceived render time. Backend traces show no token generation slowdowns.
- Rollout gating: product wants to require 95p token-inference latency < 220ms AND client-side median render < 120ms for canary -> stage promotion. Need telemetry to confirm by EOD.
- Analytics: event schema v2 is in draft but missing the `trace_id` and `rollout_bucket` fields. Without these we can’t correlate server traces with frontend session A/B buckets.

Notes by area:
UI (Arjun)
- Reproduced reflow: triggered by async image placeholder + CSS transition. Patch in PR 789 adds requestAnimationFrame debounce.
- Local perf: median render time improved from 170ms -> 95ms after patch; still failing on Chrome Canary ~210ms in some runs.
- Plan: ship patch to canary and add a client-side synthetic measurement to emit `ui_render_ms` event (see analytics notes).
- Risks: change touches modal lifecycle and focus handling; quick accessibility smoke tests needed.

Rollouts (Sofia)
- Current canary target: 5% of paid customers across us-west1 and eu-central. We observed a slightly higher failure ratio in eu-central (1.6% vs 0.4%) — likely due to older client builds.
- Gating proposal (finalizing):
  - Safety: 95th percentile server token latency (per-route) <= 220ms (1 hour window)
  - Client: median ui_render_ms <= 120ms (sampled events)
  - Errors: crash/error rate < 0.3% for canary cohort
- Action: Add gating metric to rollout pipeline (SRE/Release engineering). Need to add region-level rollout reporting in dashboard (SLO team to own alert).

Analytics / Telemetry (Leo)
- Event schema v2: added fields `trace_id`, `rollout_bucket`, `ui_render_ms`, `model_variant`. Missing in current canary; require frontend to emit `trace_id` so we can join with traces.
- Query to compute affected users (ad-hoc) provided to assess impact:
  - SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) FROM events WHERE event_type = 'console_preview' AND created_at >= '2026-03-17' AND rollout_bucket = 'canary';
- Dashboard changes: create `rollout-by-region` and `ui-render-latency` panels. Start sampling at 1% granular sampling for full traces to control cost.

Blockers:
- Frontend needs a tiny shim to propagate `trace_id` from the fetch middleware to the client instrumentation (PR pending, reviewer: Arjun).
- Release pipeline does not yet support combined gating (server + client). SRE contact: Nina. Blocking until pipeline change is in place.

Decisions made:
- We will proceed with canary patch rollout with a 5% exposure limited to us-west1 first, not EU, to limit blast radius. If metrics look good for 2 hours, expand to eu-central at 5%.
- Require frontend to emit `ui_render_ms` and `trace_id` for all canary sessions; analytics will sample 1% of full traces.

Action items (owner — due)
- Arjun: ship PR 789 with rAF debounce and the trace_id shim (target: 2026-03-18 16:00).
- Leo: add `ui_render_ms` to ingestion pipeline and a sampling rule for traces (target: 2026-03-18 18:00).
- Sofia: update rollout policy to include combined gating and request SRE to wire metric (create JIRA ENG-1543) (target: 2026-03-19).
- Maya: run accessibility smoke after canary deployment and add checklist to PR template (target: 2026-03-19).
- Nina / SRE: add combined gating to release pipeline and create alert for region skew (no later than 2026-03-20).

Follow-ups / open questions:
- Does the analytics team have capacity to increase sampling if we need deeper investigation? (Leo: yes, can bump to 5% for limited windows).
- Should we backfill `rollout_bucket` for last 48 hours for correlation? Cost estimate needed.
- Confirm that enterprise customers on dedicated instances are excluded from canary by default (policy check, Sofia).

Quick logs / artifacts referenced during meeting:
- local perf logs: /tmp/ui-bench-2026-03-18.log (Arjun)
- canary trace samples: trace://redwood/trace/2026-03-18/abc123 (Leo)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console-ui/pull/789
- Jira: ENG-1543 (rollout gating), ENG-1568 (analytics event schema)

Closing notes:
- Immediate focus: get trace_id + ui_render_ms in ingestion and ship client debounce patch. If both land, we’ll let the canary run for 2 hours and evaluate the 95p server latency + client median render.
- Checkin tomorrow 09:30 for the quick status (short async updates ok).

Raw notes / scratch ideas (brain dump):
- Consider adding a tiny browser-side cache for placeholder images to reduce reflow on repeated opens.
- Could we add a lightweight synthetic ping that measures DOM ready + image settle? Might be helpful when model latency is low and UI dominates perceived slowness.
- Make sure rollout dashboard has a toggle to exclude specific customer segments (legal/regulatory customers).
